title: Mathloutha
tagline: The “three-in-one” platter combining kabsa, mandi and madghout in a single feast.
intro: Mathloutha — literally “the mixed” — is a Saudi restaurant favourite that brings together the three great rice traditions on one platter: the tomato-rich kabsa, the smoky mandi and the pressure-cooked madghout. It is the ultimate sampler, a generous dish designed for sharing that lets everyone taste the breadth of the Kingdom's rice cookery in one sitting.

items: Mathloutha is an assembly of three separately prepared rices, plated together — not a single recipe. Prepare a portion of each of the three below (halve each recipe's quantities for a shared platter).
Follow the Chicken or Lamb Kabsa method (tomato-based, dried lime, baharat)
Follow the Chicken or Lamb Mandi method (saffron rice, finished with dukhan smoke)
Follow the Madghout method (pressure-cooked meat and rice)
Mixed roasted/grilled meats (chicken and lamb pieces)
Fried almonds, pine nuts and raisins

method: Prepare a half-batch of each of the three rices (kabsa, mandi, madghout), timing them to finish close together.
Grill or roast a mix of chicken and lamb pieces for the topping.
On a very large platter, arrange the three rices side by side in distinct sections.
Lay the mixed grilled meats over the top.
Scatter generously with fried nuts and raisins.
Serve immediately with bowls of daqoos and sahawiq.
tips: This is a project dish — plan your timings so all three rices land together, or prepare components in stages and reheat.
For catering or HORECA service, each component can be batch-cooked and assembled to order.
toServe: A grand sharing platter for a crowd — serve with multiple sauces and salads.
